clue.text: Scottish architect's protection against cats and dogs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Charles Rennie ..., the Glasgow architect and designer
second meaning: a raincoat, protection when it is raining cats and dogs

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is the possessive in the surface but works as 'is' joining the two halves. The question mark flags the idiom: raining cats and dogs means pouring rain, so the protection is a waterproof coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubberised raincoat is named after its Scottish inventor, and the famous Glasgow architect shares the surname.

clue.text: Engage in game show — and oftentimes has

indicators.note: in means the wanted word sits inside the words that follow
has means the preceding words hold the wanted word within them

parts.note: the letters sit across the join of the two words
the setter hides the same four letters a second time, across the end of this word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A contestant taking part in a TV game show, and the dash adds a muddled afterthought about oftentimes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is concealed twice: once across 'game show' and again across 'oftentimes has', where 'has' acts as a second containing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear wheels mesh or engage when their teeth interlock, so the two verbs are synonyms in mechanics.

clue.text: Crew's, so to speak, on right warship

indicators.note: so to speak means the clue word is to be heard rather than spelled as written

parts.note: crews and cruise are pronounced the same
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sailor's remark about the ship's company being in the right vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a fast, medium-sized naval vessel, so it is a type of warship.

clue.text: Lack of accommodation? Possibly renting, in case

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement of the letters among many

parts.note: all three words are taken together as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A housing shortage, with someone renting just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodation' looks like housing, which suits 'renting'; the question mark points to its other sense, being willing to compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigence is a stubborn refusal to compromise, and accommodation can mean agreeing to compromise, so lacking it fits.

clue.text: Attempts to include old people in party

indicators.note: to include means the first word wraps around the second, taking it inside

parts.note: tries are attempts
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Efforts to bring elderly people into a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories are the members of the British Conservative Party, people in a party.

clue.text: Head of state, bent into shape, pursued austerity

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of state
to crimp is to press or bend into a wavy or ridged shape

explanation.surface: A head of state, forced into line, imposed austerity measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise hard, which is what living under austerity involves.

clue.text: Cape in fashion, one of the things grudgingly worn on shoulders

definitions.text: one of the things grudgingly worn on shoulders

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
hip means trendy, in fashion

explanation.surface: A fashionable cape, the sort of garment worn on the shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'a chip on one's shoulder', a lasting grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resentful is said to have a chip on their shoulder, so it is something carried there with a grudge.

clue.text: Expert's popular photograph

parts.note: something hot is popular, in demand
a shot is a photograph

explanation.surface: An expert photographer's well-liked picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is an informal word for a person who is very skilled or successful at something.

clue.text: Rapper has a strangely different form of expression

indicators.note: strangely suggests the letters come out in an odd, unexpected order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rapper has an unusual way of expressing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase restates something in other words, a different form of expressing the same idea.

clue.text: Call for peace, say, that controls exposure when shooting occurs

definitions.text: that controls exposure when shooting occurs

parts.note: sh is the sound made to call for quiet
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: An appeal for peace while shooting is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peace' is quiet here, not the end of fighting, and 'shooting' is photography. The definition is a relative clause: the answer is a thing that controls exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera shutter opens and closes to control how long the film or sensor is exposed when a picture is taken.

clue.text: Scale of disaster? Better off over time

indicators.note: over here means lying over and around, enclosing what follows

parts.note: richer means better off financially
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Asks how bad a disaster was, then talks of being better off over time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the scale is the one used for earthquakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Richter scale measures the magnitude of earthquakes, one kind of natural disaster.

clue.text: Close attention characteristic of solution

definitions.meaning: first meaning: focusing the mind closely
second meaning: in chemistry, the amount of a substance dissolved in a liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' suggests solving the crossword, which needs close attention; here it is a chemical mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both mental focus and the strength of a dissolved substance in a chemical mixture.

clue.text: Political skill, an asset this MP badly needed

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together poorly, in the wrong order, and needed leans on it

parts.note: the letters of these four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomatic skill is a quality this particular MP was sorely lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly needed' reads as 'sorely wanted' but 'badly' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Statesmanship is the skill and wisdom shown in managing public affairs, a kind of political ability.

clue.text: Director of players refashioned team's brand

indicators.note: refashioned means made into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports team's manager has rebranded the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests a sports team but means musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandmaster conducts a band, directing its musicians, who are players of instruments.

clue.text: A peasant sent back by hospital once more

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a serf was a feudal peasant
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A sick peasant is turned away from hospital yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew or again, starting over, which is what once more expresses.

clue.text: See terms reorganised as one

definitions.note: one of the terms just mentioned

indicators.note: reorganised means arranged again in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university notice that several terms are being merged into one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'terms' in the fodder: the answer is one term, a half-year at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year academic period, one of the terms into which a college year is divided.

clue.text: Landed up in argument, producing knife

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a set-to is a quarrel or fight

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lit is a past tense of light, to land or alight

explanation.surface: Someone ends up in a row that turns violent when a knife is drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: To light on something is to land on it, so 'landed' gives the past tense. The reversed word goes inside the argument after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Some beers for men on board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: beers drawn from the cask
second meaning: the board game whose pieces are called men

explanation.walkthrough: 'Men on board' suggests sailors on a ship, but it is the board game known in America as checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer is drawn from a cask, and draughts is the British name for the board game checkers, played with pieces called men.

clue.text: In a fight scene, is getting up

indicators.note: in places one word inside the following phrase

parts.note: a ring, the arena where boxers fight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film director describing an actor rising in the middle of a fight scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fight scene' suggests a film; it is the boxing ring, with the word is placed after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arising means getting up, as from bed or a chair.

clue.text: Poles following articles in foreign capital

indicators.note: following means placed after the words that come next in the clue

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people coming after some newspaper stories set in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it means the ends of the earth's axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, foreign from the setter's British point of view.

clue.text: Inspire some children thus excited

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Getting children thrilled is a way to inspire them.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse someone is to fill them with enthusiasm, which is to inspire them.

clue.text: Optimistic in the lead, then defeated

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, in the lead
beat means defeated

explanation.surface: A competitor feels hopeful while ahead, then loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat is an informal word for cheerful and hopeful about the future.

clue.text: Changed plane in haste, a kind of Jumbo

indicators.note: changed means altered into something else, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller hurriedly switching to a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' and 'Jumbo' together suggest a Boeing 747; Jumbo was also a famous elephant, and the name became a nickname for any elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo is a nickname for an elephant, and the Asian elephant is one of the species.

clue.text: Stayed, right? Wrong on both counts

definitions.text: Stayed, right? Wrong on both counts

parts.note: surface reading: someone checking that they are correct that a person remained
setter's reading: the answer is the opposite of stayed and also the opposite of right

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is one word that is the opposite of both: as a verb it means departed, and as a direction it is the other side from right.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means went away, the reverse of remained, and names the side opposite the right hand.

clue.text: Spear I had dropped in river

indicators.note: dropped in means put down inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they lost a spear into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune.

clue.text: English piano I preserve for discriminating consumer

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
taken as written
to cure meat or fish is to preserve it by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: Someone preserving an English piano for a choosy buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like looking after the piano; it is curing food, which fits the gourmet.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person with refined taste in food and drink, a discerning eater.

clue.text: North European port held by frigates

indicators.note: held by means contained within the next word

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A northern port occupied by warships.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga, the capital of Latvia, is a major port on the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Accidental detachment

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a group of soldiers sent off from the main force

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a phrase about something coming loose by accident; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Contingent as an adjective means happening by chance; as a noun it is a body of troops forming part of a larger force.
